status: implemented bounded helper; wired by flac-transform.ts into the public FLAC backend

exports.processFlacAudioFilters: (frames: AsyncIterable<AudioFrameData>, compiled: CompiledFlacAudioFilters, options: {resources: ResourceContext, signal: AbortSignal, maxFrameBytes: number, inputFormat?: AudioPadFormat}) => AsyncIterable<AudioFrameData>

compiled: Extends existing AudioFilterChain without changing semantics; encoderSampleFormat is the requested output hint. plan(inputSamples: bigint, inputRate: number, inputFormat: AudioSampleFormat) returns finite samples, buffers, stages, outputRate, sampleFormat (filter output), encoderSampleFormat, requiresScalarRounding. Existing outputSamples/outputSampleRate/resolvedSampleFormat/packetSections also remain available.
input: AudioFrameData, not FlacDecodedFrame; backend must supply accounted packed/planar PCM frames with stable rate/channels/layout/sampleFormat and preserve sample-aligned contiguous timestamps for buffering filters. Optional inputFormat snapshots decoded source rate/channels/layout/sampleFormat/pts before awaits, enables configured empty padding, and must agree with nonempty source format.
lifetime: Single consumer; each output is borrowed until next()/return(). Do not retain frames unless copied into independently accounted memory. Producer owns/releases input memory. Always close iterator on early stop.
memory: Before filtering first input (or before opening source when inputFormat is supplied), reserveExternalMemory acquires a conservative resident envelope: maxFrameBytes per allocating scalar node, two bounded slots per asetnsamples node, one bounded packet per apad node. Every actual allocation must fit min(maxFrameBytes, resources.budget.maxBufferBytes); finite padding uses min(packet_size, finite tail bound), not the configured packet_size alone. Reservations survive yields and release on EOF/error/abort/return. Source and separately owned PCM encoding/output writer allocations are not double-accounted here and must be accounted by backend.
cancellation: Either options.signal or resources.signal cancels; pending next()/return() are abort-aware and late rejection is observed. Uncooperative source cleanup can finish after cancellation and remains producer-owned.
integration: flac-transform.ts imports this helper directly, compiles before output creation, and executes two bounded passes with shared Core resources: count actual transformed samples, then independently encode/mux through the atomic output group. Do not substitute encoderSampleFormat for filter output sampleFormat. The backend enforces -cpuflags 0 when scalar rounding is required. The helper plan remains available for callers with an exact selected decoded count.
limitations: Helper itself does not resample/remix/evaluate graphs or invoke Native; separate backend stages own supported transforms
Conservative envelope may reject budgets that a finer per-allocation allocator could fit
Header count must be computed from actual selected input count, not unknown STREAMINFO total
